gap._description: No confirmed rust emission gaps remain after the 2026-08-28 review: union_item and associated_type (previously emitting NOTHING) are now handled and fixture-pinned; differential ripgrep:rust is 0 missing / 0 unexplained at the pinned floor.

decisions.question: Rust has no class-based inheritance; trait supertraits and trait implementations are the hierarchy.
decisions.resolution: TRAIT SEMANTICS: trait supertrait bounds (trait Foo: Bar + Baz) emit extends; impl<Trait> for Type emits implements from the TYPE to the TRAIT. No overrides edge exists by design (no method shadowing across impls).

decisions.question: macro_rules! bodies parse as opaque token trees (token_tree/token_repetition/metavariable); expansion is not performed.
decisions.resolution: DECLARED LIMITATION: macro invocations emit a calls edge to the macro NAME (format! -> format), never expanded bodies; macro_definition emits a Macro symbol. Expansions are out of scope for a static analyzer.

decisions.question: Rust completeness scope is tied to the pinned tree-sitter-rust grammar.
decisions.resolution: The inventory is exhaustive for the pinned grammar; future grammar drift requires a new inventory review.

decisions.question: RSD1 (cargo+ripgrep census, 2026-09-05): qualified_calls were accumulated in a map keyed by BARE method name, so same-named methods on different types (Alpha.run / Beta.run; 21 deserialize methods in one file) shared one union payload — 410 buckets / 1,313 symbols / 749 excess entries.
decisions.resolution: Payloads attach DIRECTLY to the enclosing fn/method symbol at call time (java/groovy/cpp family contract). Payload now equals exactly the symbol's own call set; cross-type pollution structurally impossible. Pinned by rust/qualified-calls-ownership (per-owner notIncludes).

decisions.question: RSD2: the attach guard `!ctx.metadata.errors` wiped qualified_calls from EVERY function in any file with a parse error — 519 error files / 4,620 functions silently lost payloads (cargo's own frontmatter.rs: 40 fns from 18 single-token str![[r# raw-string grammar limits).
decisions.resolution: Whole-file suppression removed; per-symbol direct attach is precise under ERROR recovery (recovered code keeps the real enclosing symbol). Error files keep their functions' payloads. Pinned by rust/error-file-payload (fixture with a deliberate error).

decisions.question: RSD3: `struct Foo` + every `impl Foo` block created a symbol named Foo with the SAME id 'Foo' (also field vs same-named accessor) — 2,852 duplicate ids across 271 files. Id-keyed graph consumers dedupe silently, dropping distinct declarations.
decisions.resolution: Per-file usedIds set in createSymbol: first claim keeps the plain id, later same-(owner,name) declarations get deterministic '#N' suffixes (Alpha, Alpha#2, Alpha#3). Ids are in-memory only (not persisted); ownerName stays the type anchor for graph edges. Pinned by rust/qualified-calls-ownership expectUniqueIds + id pins.

decisions.question: RSD4: macro invocations emit calls edges (toSymbol macro:name) but never reached qualified_calls — a function whose body only invokes macros (format!/println!) had an empty payload despite real call sites.
decisions.resolution: Macro invocations attach `macro:name` payload entries (same vocabulary as their toSymbol), so payload == emitted call set per function. Pinned by rust/qualified-calls-ownership (second / macro:format).

decisions.question: RSD5 (cargo census, 2026-09-05): `self.x = v` (assignment_expression) and `self.x += v` (compound_assignment_expr) field expressions on the LEFT are WRITES, but the field_expression branch emitted uses unconditionally — 1,076 bogus edges across cargo+ripgrep. The oracle derives no uses truth, so no differential could catch it (cpp/ruby waves fixed the same class; rust never got the gate).
decisions.resolution: Span-compare gate (fresh-wrapper safe): a field_expression that is namedChild(0) of assignment_expression/compound_assignment_expr emits nothing; read-modify-write keeps its edge via the RHS occurrence. Pure reads unchanged. Pinned by rust/qualified-calls-ownership forbidRelationships (set_name/bump_count).

decisions.question: RSD6a (2026-09-05): `use std::{env, io, path::{Path, PathBuf}}` binds Path/PathBuf, but the inner scoped_use_list child fell through collect() and its leaves were silently DROPPED — 65 declarations across cargo+ripgrep (7,367 use-decls audited).
decisions.resolution: The use_list collector now recurses into nested scoped_use_list children and appends their leaf bindings (the submodule name is never bound unless listed). Pinned by rust/use-list-imports (module std, items env/io/Path/PathBuf).

decisions.question: RSD6b (2026-09-05): `use {std::sync::Arc, std::time::Duration};` has no shared module prefix, but the single-row aggregation fabricated module 'Arc, Duration' (items joined) — 28 declarations across cargo+ripgrep.
decisions.resolution: Top-level group imports now emit ONE import row per binding, each with its full module path (std::sync::Arc / std::time::Duration). Same-prefix rows still merge into one. Pinned by rust/use-list-imports per-binding rows + forbidImports 'Read, File'.

decisions.question: RSD7 (2026-09-05 post-close re-review, framework-family gap): detectedFrameworks only fired on actix route macros (#[get]/#[post]/...) — a real file using #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] + #[tokio::main] yielded detectedFrameworks=[]. The cpp/python family contract populates detectedFrameworks from code signals; rust never got the non-actix attribute paths.
decisions.resolution: handleAttribute now detects serde (bare-word scan of the derive body for Serialize/Deserialize — regex-free since #798, genuinely replaced by `hasBareWord` under an equivalence proof), clap (Parser/Subcommand/Args/ValueEnum), thiserror (crate-qualified marker only — bare Error never implies it), tokio (#[tokio::main|test], flavor), axum/rocket (crate:: path in the attribute), tracing (::instrument). Name-scoped, so std-only derives (Debug/Clone) cannot false-positive. Corpus sanity: cargo+ripgrep 1,481 files -> serde 55 / thiserror 10 / tracing 29, zero garbage names; zero clap/tokio is honest (both repos hand-roll CLI and sync). Pinned by rust/relationship-kinds expectFrameworks [actix_web, serde, tokio].

decisions.question: Rust review (#736): the analyzer emitted NO bare-identifier edges (`LIMIT + GLOBAL` produced zero relationships) while the oracle audited only calls/member reads — a both-sides blind spot (the `uses` label, like `references`, sat OUTSIDE the F5 comparison for rust at the time — #798 later added both to the allowlist with independent oracles, see R15/R16).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-11): file-visible VALUE reads emit Uses (const/static/fn/enum-variant/struct/enum/union/type + use-imported leaves; qualified variant leaves included as the deliberate Rust difference; declaration positions, callees, member leaves, qualified non-leaves, macro/attribute/use paths, LHS writes, where-bounds excluded; shadowing via per-function pattern bindings incl. destructured/match/for/closure params). Fixture rust/bare-value-reads + mutants rust/drop-bare-uses, rust/reemit-shadowed-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust review (#736): explicit `where T: Clone` emitted references to the BOUND type parameter (locally bound, not a file type).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-11): bare-identifier bounds matching the enclosing generic params are skipped; real path bounds (`String: PartialEq`, relationship-kinds pin) still emit. Fixture forbid (bare-value-reads) + mutant rust/reemit-where-param-refs CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust second review (#736): `Self { x }` and `Self::new()` targeted the literal `Self`, which the deferred in-file filter dropped — Self-construction was entirely silent.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-11): Self resolves to the enclosing impl type (struct literals, ::new receivers, bare PascalCase targets; trait bodies without impl keep prior behavior). Fixture rust/construction-exports + mutant rust/drop-self-construction CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust second review (#736): `pub(crate)`/`pub(super)` items and members of private modules entered the export list as public API (struct/trait/enum/use lacked even the fn/mod/variable !parent rule).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED (2026-09-11): exports require unrestricted `pub` at true file top level (members ride Contains, matching the fn/mod/variable contract); symbol visibility fields untouched. Fixture rust/construction-exports + mutant rust/restore-restricted-exports CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust second review (#736): `pub use std::io::Read` exports under the full module path rather than the local binding.
decisions.resolution: KEPT BY DESIGN (2026-09-11): the path form is unambiguous about provenance and satisfies the uniqueness invariant; renaming to local bindings is a consumer-facing change for its own wave. Probed, no defect found.

decisions.question: Rust extreme review (2026-09-13): the match-arm binding sweep covered six pattern node types but not the `match_pattern` wrapper or bare binding patterns — `v => v` with a same-named file value emitted junk uses (probe-verified false positive on both the pattern site and the body read).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: the arm's `pattern` field subtree is swept with match semantics (bare identifiers included); the arm body is untouched (its reads are values). Fixture rust/bare-value-reads expects arm_binds->VAL (constant-pattern read) and forbids arm_binds->v; mutant rust/reemit-arm-binding-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust extreme review (2026-09-13): closure parameters were never collected into the binding set despite the documented contract (closures folded in), so `|G| G + 1` with a file const G emitted a junk use (probe-verified).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: closure_parameters patterns bind with declaration semantics into the enclosing function's set (closure-wide precision is a documented flow-insensitive residual, same class as cross-arm reads). Fixture forbids closure_binds->VAL and expects the post-closure LIMIT read; mutant rust/closure-param-reads CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust extreme review (2026-09-13): `use std::io::Read` bound NOTHING in the R1 name set (only bare/braced/aliased leaves were collected) while the import ROW was recorded correctly — every read of a plain-path import stayed silent (probe-verified missing pair).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: direct-path and group-leaf scoped paths bind their last segment (brace-group prefixes bind nothing, matching the import rows). Fixture expects capped->MAX; mutant rust/drop-scoped-use-leaf CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust extreme review (2026-09-13): `const _ : u32 = 0;` (valid Rust) minted a `_` Variable symbol (GO5/Z8 class, probe-verified).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: blank names skipped in handleVariable and in the value-owner inventory. Fixture forbids any `_` symbol; mutant rust/blank-symbol CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust extreme review (2026-09-13): rust emitted NO declared-type references at all (only where-bounds) — the one family-standard surface it lacked (param/return/field/alias types).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: extractRustDeclaredTypeRefs emits references for every named type mentioned in parameter types, return types, struct/union field types, enum variant field types (tuple and struct forms), const/static types and alias right-hand sides. Primitives/lifetimes auto-excluded by node type; generic parameter lists are declarations (the R8 generic->T forbid guards the same name); where-clauses stay with R8; body-local annotations and turbofish args are a documented boundary; Self resolves via the enclosing impl type (D2 rule) and is otherwise skipped. references was an UNCOMPARED label for rust when this ruling was written; #798 (rust review, 2026-09-24) closed that gap: deriveRustDeclaredTypeRefs mirrors this rule for rule and `references` joined the rust F5 allowlist, so the whole declared-type surface is now compared over both corpora in full extent (0 missing / 0 unexplained). Fixture rust/declared-type-refs (9 edges); mutant rust/drop-declared-type-refs CAUGHT.

decisions.question: Rust extreme review (2026-09-13): the D2 analyzer resolves Self to the enclosing impl type, but the differential oracle emitted raw Self (struct literals) and silence (calls) — cargo rustdoc.rs + manifest/mod.rs lanes showed one disagreement each surfacing as MISSING Self + UNEXPLAINED RealType pairs.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + LANE-GATED: deriveRustEdges mirrors D2 exactly (enclosing-impl resolution with the analyzer fallback rule: struct literals keep raw Self, calls drop it; exported for direct verification like the zig/cpp oracles). Verified 0/0 on all three divergent files directly plus fresh cargo + ripgrep rotations 100%/0/0. Analyzer side pinned by construction-exports (Self literal, Self::new, and new bare Self(..) wrap->Wrap case); mutant rust/drop-self-construction extended to Wrap.

decisions.question: Rust review #798 (2026-09-24, ripgrep full extent): a TUPLE struct declares its fields exactly as a named one does (`struct StandardStream(StandardStreamKind);`), but has no `field_declaration` child — the types sit directly in an `ordered_field_declaration_list`, a shape only the ENUM branch walked. Every tuple-struct field type was therefore invisible: measured 13 missing `references` edges over 10 ripgrep files (StandardStream(StandardStreamKind), LiteralStrategy(fnv::HashMap<..>), IgnoreMatch(IgnoreMatchInner), Glob(GlobInner), Override(Gitignore), LineTerminator(..), ByteSet(BitSet), RegexCaptures(..), HyperlinkConfig(Arc), NiceDuration(Duration), MmapChoice(..)).
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: the struct/union branch handles `ordered_field_declaration_list` like a field_declaration body (visibility modifiers and names are not types; only type_identifier leaves resolve), so a tuple field's type leaves emit references just as a named field's do. The R8 generic-parameter exclusion and the enum tuple-variant path are untouched; the union case stays on its named-field path (a `union` with tuple fields does not parse). Fixture rust/tuple-struct-field-types (7 pins incl. the Generic<T>(T, Inner) exclusion and a Unit struct forbid); mutant rust/drop-tuple-struct-field-types CAUGHT. Full extent after the fix: ripgrep 0 missing / 0 unexplained, cargo 0/0.

decisions.node_type: where-clause bound target spelling + generic-parameter climb
decisions.question: Rust review #798 (2026-09-24, cargo full extent): two holes in R8's own words ('the enclosing generic params') and one in its target spelling. (a) `function_signature_item` — a TRAIT method declaration, which has no body — was missing from the item list, so the climb skipped the signature and stopped at the trait, whose type_parameters are the TRAIT's: a where clause on a method signature never saw the method's own parameters (`where F: FnOnce() -> ...;` emitted references->F, exactly the locally-bound name R8 excludes inside a function_item; cargo once.rs, paths.rs, package_id_spec.rs). (b) The climb took the FIRST enclosing item and stopped, so a bound naming an OUTER parameter (`impl<N, E> Graph<N, E>` with `where N: Borrow<Q>` on a method) was read as a file type (cargo src/util/graph.rs). (c) The bounded side published RAW TEXT, so `where T::Err: Display` yielded the target `T::Err`, `where <T as FromStr>::Err: Display` yielded `<T as FromStr>::Err`, and `where anyhow::Error: From<E>` yielded the MODULE `anyhow` — targets no consumer can resolve (the c/cpp #924 name-surface class); a lifetime bound (`where 'a: 's`) published `'a`, which is not a symbol at all.
decisions.resolution: FIXED + GATED: the climb walks the WHOLE enclosing-item chain (every enclosing generic item binds) and includes `function_signature_item`; the bounded side contributes its scoped path's `name` leaf (`anyhow::Error`->Error, `T::Err`->Err, `<T as X>::Err`->Err — never a module prefix or raw text), a lone `type_identifier`, and nothing for a lifetime subtree. `String: PartialEq` (the relationship-kinds pin) is unchanged; the same rule holds on the declared-type side by construction (it reads type_identifier leaves only). Fixture `rust/where-clause-bounds-798` pairs each hole with the exact pre-fix emission it must refuse (printed from the pre-fix rule by `script/m14/tmp/rust-798-wherebounds.ts`: `F`, `N`, `String`, `anyhow::Error`), and mutants `rust/revert-where-clause-climb` and `rust/where-bound-raw-text` are EACH caught by that fixture alone. Full extent after the fix: cargo 0 missing / 0 unexplained (was 1 unexplained at the `where anyhow::Error: From<E>` site), ripgrep 0/0.

decisions.node_type: published name surface (impl targets + raw identifiers)
decisions.status: FIXED (2026-09-24, rust #798 round 2) — (1) fixed and gated; (2) RULED, with the ruling enforced by the same gate
decisions.question: Rust review #798 (2026-09-24): two published-name classes are source TEXT rather than a NAME. (1) An `impl` whose target is not a nominal type publishes the target's type text as the impl SYMBOL name (`&'a mut P`, `[u8]`, `(T, U)`, `&mut ProcessBuilder`), and the same text rides two further surfaces — the `implements` relationship's SOURCE and `Self` resolution inside the impl's methods (which is why cargo emits `references` to `&mut ProcessBuilder` from `env`/`arg`/`current_dir`: the methods' `-> Self` resolves to the impl target). Measured through the production entry: ripgrep 10 impl-symbol rows, cargo 21 impl-symbol rows + 6 such `references` rows. (2) A RAW IDENTIFIER is published with its escape prefix in BOTH the symbol and every target (`fn r#try` / `self.r#try(..)` / `StderrReader::r#async(..)`): ripgrep 1 symbol + 1 target, cargo 2 symbols + 11 targets. Neither class is an unknown symbol or a missing relationship: the raw-identifier surface is internally CONSISTENT (symbol and targets agree, so it resolves), and the impl-target surface is honest type text. Both are the c/cpp #924 name-surface class, which F14 (`script/m14/verify-name-surface-924.ts`) gates for c/cpp only — rust is not covered.
decisions.resolution: CLOSED 2026-09-24, both halves. (1) THE IMPL-TARGET CLASS IS FIXED. Rule: an impl's published name is the implemented type's NOMINAL name, because a reference/pointer/parenthesized wrapper is transparent — `&mut ProcessBuilder` IS the type `ProcessBuilder` — and the pre-fix `stripGenerics(typeNode.text)` published SOURCE TEXT as a name on three surfaces at once (the impl SYMBOL, the `implements` edge's SOURCE, and, through `Self`, every `references` TARGET inside the block). Measured conviction that forced it: the M60 target-spelling census on the pre-fix analyzer read `anomalies=6 {"whitespace":6}` — 5x `references -> "&mut ProcessBuilder"` and 1x `references -> "&mut Execs"`, all at cargo/crates/cargo-test-support/src/lib.rs — and the register's `clean` had been a DRAW artifact (the violating file is absent from cargo's canonical 40-file draw; script/m14/tmp/rust-798-draw-check.ts). For a type with NO nominal name (a slice `[u8]`, a tuple `(T, U)`, a unit, a never type, a fn pointer, `dyn Trait`, `<T as Trait>::Assoc`) the decisions the entry listed as competing are now settled in the R7 direction: the impl BLOCK takes the family's declared synthetic `anonymous_impl` (c's `anonymous_struct`/`anonymous_union`/`anonymous_enum`, cpp's `anonymous`) with the type's own spelling kept in `metadata.implementedType`, while `Self` RESOLUTION takes ABSENCE — the honest state is absence, not a placeholder, and the synthetic block name is never substituted for the type in a TARGET position. The nominal base is NOT used where no nominal base exists (`[u8]` does not become `u8`: that would be an identity lie), and the trait name is not used either (it collides with the trait's own symbol in the same file — `impl ToPkgId for (T, U)` sits next to `trait ToPkgId` in cargo/crates/resolver-tests/src/helpers.rs). Path QUALIFICATION is preserved on the symbol (`std::io::Error` stays qualified — the deferred constructor filter reads in-file symbol names, and flattening it added 12 spurious `instantiates` edges on ripgrep alone) while `Self` resolves to the LEAF (`Error`), which is a `references` target by the #419-B leaf-target contract. Gated by: fixture validation/m14/fixtures/rust/impl-target-name-surface-798 (4 shapes + the `calls -> Self` follow-through, every forbid proven to FAIL on revert by re-deriving the pre-fix rule from the tree — script/m14/tmp/rust-798-fixture-dump.ts with BB_PRE_R10=1), mutant `rust/revert-impl-target-wrapper-name` (CAUGHT), and the F14 name-surface gate EXTENDED TO RUST (`script/m14/verify-name-surface-924.ts`: 18,658 name-bearing targets + 4,069 symbols over ripgrep 110 + cargo 400, 0 violations, both rust checks tripping on the pre-fix rule). A/B at both corpora (script/m14/tmp/rust-798-r10-ab.ts): ripgrep 4 symbols + 43 relationships changed, cargo 9/12 + 62/60, every row a rename of the same root. (2) THE RAW-IDENTIFIER CLASS IS RULED, NOT RENAMED, and the ruling is the opposite of what the entry assumed. A raw identifier keeps its `r#` prefix on BOTH the symbol and everything that targets it (`r#try`, `r#async`), and the F14 gate DECLARES it as the identifier's own accepted spelling for a reason that is decisive: the prefix is the only way that identifier can be written in source, so stripping it would publish `try`/`async` — bare KEYWORDS, which the gate now refuses BY NAME (R2 of F14). The class is internally consistent (symbol and target agree, so it resolves; refTargetNotName 0) and it is not an unknown symbol. Measured: ripgrep 1 symbol + 1 target, cargo 2 symbols + 11 targets. (3) WHAT THE ROUND ALSO FOUND, because gating is what found it: `calls -> "Self"` — the KEYWORD published as a callee name, 6 rows on cargo (`Ok(Self(name))` in cargo-util-schemas/src/manifest/mod.rs, `Self(ProcessEnv)` in build-rs/src/input.rs), which the census could not see because `Self` is well-SPELLED (R10's classes are about spelling) and the differential could not see because its truth derives from the same rule. `Self(..)` now names the enclosing impl type's constructor exactly as `Name(..)` does, a trait default body (no impl to resolve) omits the edge, and the fixture forbids `calls -> Self` with its own mutant (rust/reemit-self-callee-target, CAUGHT). Full-extent verification at final bytes: F5 0 missing / 0 unexplained on both corpora (6,309 truth edges on ripgrep, 41,793 on cargo), F3 17/17 rust fixtures, F4 32/32 rust mutants CAUGHT, target-spelling census `--lane rust --sample 2285` clean (1,351 files, 182,977 relationships, 0 anomalies, 0 separator triples), tsc clean.

decisions.question: RUST-MR: an M60 line audit, exact and per label over 450 files of five real corpora (74,584 relationships), found 279 `uses` edges whose claimed line is not a name-bearing line. Every one was a position that DECLARES rather than reads, and each was a container shape the R1 read sweep's guards did not enumerate: (1) a macro INVOCATION's `macro` field is a callee (the callee guard tested `call_expression` only) — 269 sites, and because `calls -> bail` also published, one site carried the same name under two labels; (2) a trait method DECLARATION is a `function_signature_item`, absent from the `isItemNamePosition` switch — 10 sites, and at cargo-test-support/src/lib.rs:1477 the edge was a SELF-EDGE (`uses current_dir -> current_dir`); (3) a fn-pointer TYPE's parameter declares and has no body, so no bound-name set excluded it — 2 sites. An imported FUNCTION called by name published `calls` only throughout, which is what made (1) look like a macro quirk rather than a missing guard.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): a declaration position is not a read, and the three container shapes are named explicitly rather than left to a list that grows by accident. (1) A macro invocation's NAME is a callee: the guard climbs `scoped_identifier`/`generic_function` and matches the `macro` FIELD by span, exactly as the call-callee guard does, so a path macro (`std::eprintln!`) is covered and the invocation's ARGUMENTS are untouched — they are reads and keep publishing (fixture control: `sum_all!(items, LIMIT)` still emits `uses -> LIMIT`). (2) `function_signature_item` joins the declaration-position switch. (3) A parameter whose `parameters` node sits in a `bare_function_type`/`function_type`/`parenthesized_type` is a declaration; a real function's parameters were already excluded by the per-function bound-name set, and a type's parameters had no such set. Fixtures macro-callee-read and declaration-position-reads (both FAIL proved pre-fix by disabling the guards), mutants rust/reemit-macro-callee-uses and rust/reemit-declaration-position-reads CAUGHT. THE ORACLE MIRRORED IT, and that is the part worth recording: `deriveRustBareUses`'s only macro rule skipped identifiers under a macro DEFINITION, stopping at `macro_invocation`, so it derived the same fabricated read — F5 compared a fabrication against a fabrication and reported 0 unexplained. A shared blind spot is not agreement (the R14 lesson, applied to a label R14 never touched).

decisions.question: RUST-MR: the lane's line gate (M59.A7) is deliberately a NECESSARY condition — 'a pass is NOT proof the line is the exact call node' — so it cannot carry the M60 claim. The exact per-label claim is: the line on an edge is the line of the node that BEARS the name the edge publishes. Measured 2026-09-29 over 450 files of five real corpora, deriving the expected line from the tree alone: 7 labels, 74,584 relationships, 0 line-less and 0 off-name after RUST-D13, with ONE class that is not a defect: 825 `references`/`instantiates`/`calls` edges where the published target is the ENCLOSING IMPL TYPE (RUST-D12's `Self` resolution) and the claimed line is the `Self` SITE, not the impl head where the type is declared.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): (1) The per-label line contract is CLEAN for all seven labels — calls 40,618, contains 10,011 (each edge's line is the member's own DECLARATION line, a stronger question than 'the token appears'), extends 40, implements 1,234, instantiates 1,879, references 11,903, uses 8,899. Instrument: script/m14/tmp/rust-line-audit.ts, expected lines derived from the tree (`scoped_identifier`'s `name` FIELD, `struct_expression`'s `name`, a `field_expression`'s `field`, a `use` path's leaf, an `impl_item`'s `trait`, a `trait_item`'s bound) and never read back from the analyzer. (2) The `Self` case is RULED, not excused: the line is the SITE of the `Self` token, because the alternative collapses hundreds of distinct sites onto the impl head and destroys the site information the line exists to carry. The 825 are COUNTED and reported on every run, so the class cannot grow unnoticed. (3) The instrument's own four defects are on the record, because an audit that cannot state a rule reports its own ignorance as analyzer loss: it did not implement RUST-D13's guards (279 phantoms), it excluded a const/static's INITIALIZER as if the whole node declared (7 phantoms), its path-segment helper did not recurse into a `match_pattern` (795 phantoms), and it enumerated path container types one at a time instead of taking every `::` path in the file. Every one of the 279 real findings was re-adjudicated against source before a single line of the analyzer changed.

decisions.question: RUST-MR: `for<'de> Deserialize<'de>` — the lifetime-generic supertrait idiom — wraps its bound type in a `higher_ranked_trait_bound` node, so the supertrait extraction's direct-child test never matched and the bound was published by NOBODY. serde's own `pub trait DeserializeOwned: for<'de> Deserialize<'de> {}` published nothing. The F5 oracle had the mirror-image bug on the same construct: it read the BINDER's text and FABRICATED `extends -> "for"`, a bound no source line names. So both sides were wrong in opposite directions, which is why the row surfaced as one MISSING and the real supertrait was invisible on both sides.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): a higher-ranked bound IS a bound — the extraction descends past the `for<…>` binder to the type node and publishes `extends` on that node's line; and the binder's `for` is NOT a name, so the oracle's text path is replaced by the same descent and can never derive `for` again. Measured: 3 higher-ranked bounds in 2 files across 2,598, and this is the only construct where a supertrait bound is named in source and absent from the graph. A `where`-clause higher-ranked bound stays a WHERE bound (R8's surface) and must not become an `extends` — fixture row. Fixture higher-ranked-bounds (FAIL proved pre-fix) + mutant rust/drop-higher-ranked-bounds CAUGHT, and the edge survives the store seam (extends 10/10 in the round trip).

decisions.question: RUST-MR: while closing RUST-D13 the lane's F5 oracle produced three unexplained rows that turned out to be the ORACLE being narrower than the analyzer in three independent ways: a bare uppercase CALLEE (`Ok(())`), a SCOPED struct literal, and a struct literal whose type was imported under a LOWERCASE alias (`use libc::ucred;` then `let mut ucred = ucred { … }` — five sites in tokio). Each was an analyzer edge the oracle derived no truth for, so F5's '0 unexplained' was partly arithmetic luck rather than a matched contract.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): a construction is a construction whatever its type is SPELLED, so the oracle mirrors the analyzer's SHAPE rule for `struct_expression` (the leaf-casing test goes, the `Self` resolution stays) and derives the bare-uppercase-callee construction. The casing test had been carrying a cargo-lane lesson (CARGO-D1, a qualified literal whose text starts lowercase) that the LEAF already handles — the case test and the leaf rule were solving one problem twice, and the case test was the copy that lost tokio's five rows. REGISTERED, one row, both readings defensible: `instantiates -> Ok` for the PRELUDE's `Ok` is emitted by the analyzer while the oracle filters non-local constructions per the analyzer's own deferred rule, so exactly one row in 2,598 files disagrees (serde_core/src/ser/mod.rs). Left as it is: changing a side on a single row is how a contract starts drifting in two directions at once, and the row is enumerated by script/m14/tmp/rust-disagreement.ts on every run.

decisions.question: RUST-MR: a per-FORM declaration census over 450 files of five real corpora reported function-local `const` at 0/43 and `static` at 0/22, while module-level `const` was 200/200 and associated ones 15/15 — so the spec's `handled_verified` claim for both node types was true at one scope and false at another. The cause is a one-token over-reach: the guard that skips declarations inside a function body tested the PARENT's kind, so it covered `let_declaration`, `const_item` AND `static_item` while its own comment says "function-local `let` bindings are execution artifacts" — the only one of the three the rule is true for. The same census also printed `extern crate` at 0/18, which this round establishes was the CENSUS's wrong channel, not a defect: rust puts module dependencies in `imports`, and `use` publishes no symbol and no `references` edge either, because `references` is the TYPE surface (R13 declared types, R8 where-bounds, behaviour/derive).
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): a function-local `const`/`static` is a DECLARATION — a named value with a type, an initializer and a line — and publishes a symbol owned by the enclosing function with its `contains` edge on its own line; `let` keeps the skip, because a local binding declares nothing outside its body (M11.11's closure boundary) and a symbol for it would be noise. The CHANNEL is part of the ruling: a form's coverage must be measured on the channel its contract uses, so the census reports two — symbol for ten forms, `imports` for `use` and `extern crate`. After both corrections every live form reads 100.0% (fn 7352, struct 808, enum 200, trait 79, mod 462, type alias 529, const 243, static 37, macro_rules 147, use 2553, extern crate 18) with `union` reported as having NO live site rather than as OK. Fixture function-local-consts (FAIL proved pre-fix) + mutant rust/drop-function-local-consts CAUGHT. CORRECTION this supersedes: the master review's F-4 called `extern crate` "publishes no symbol and no `references` edge" a defect; the edge half was wrong — `use` publishes none either — so it was a census artifact, and both the review and the census now say so.

decisions.node_type: n/a — PERF (the flagged per-function body walk)
decisions.question: RUST-MR: the fifth review left `collectFunctionBindings` on the record as "walks one full subtree per `function_item` (O(fns × file)) — the likely scaling term, pre-existing, untouched". A term named likely that has never been measured is a standing assumption, and the lane's own perf evidence could not settle it: ms/kB by quartile (Q1 116.6 → Q4 3.64) is a composition artifact, which that review itself said.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-29): MEASURED and RULED OUT as a scaling defect, with a ladder built to isolate the term (script/m14/tmp/rust-perf-ladder.ts, warmup + median of 3 with the spread printed, because the first single-run reading was noise: arm A read 466ms at N=50 and 284ms at N=100). Arm A (N sibling functions) is flat in ms/def — 2.58 / 4.03 / 2.84 / 2.53 at N=50/100/200/400 — so there is no term in the function COUNT. Arm B (one function, N statements) is linear. Arm C is the case that makes the walks non-disjoint, because an `impl` block inside a function body is legal Rust: N functions each holding an impl of N methods, 40,200 definitions in 1.8MB, still flat at 2.05 → 1.44 ms/def across a 15.8× increase. The single-run version of that table read as quadratic (×5.35 for ×2 N); the medians say linear. The term is real, bounded, and not a defect — so the note is retired with a measurement instead of being carried forward as folklore. Real corpora, bucketed by DEFINITION count (not size, which is what produced the old composition artifact): ms/def 26.9 / 7.0 / 12.4 / 9.6 over quartiles of 1 / 3 / 8 / 21 definitions, where Q1 is the fixed cost of one walk on a 1.8KB file.

decisions.question: RUST-MR: RUST-D13's declaration-position rule was one level too shallow. It covered a fn-pointer TYPE's parameter and a trait method's own NAME, but not a trait method SIGNATURE's PARAMETERS — and those declare for the same reason: `collectFunctionBindings` collects `function_item` only, so a bodiless `function_signature_item` has NO bound-name set and its parameter names fell through to the read sweep. Found only at FULL extent: cargo's `src/compiler/mod.rs:142-143` published `uses -> on_stdout_line` and `uses -> on_stderr_line` for `fn exec(&self, …, on_stdout_line: &mut dyn FnMut(&str) -> CargoResult<()>, …) -> CargoResult<()>;` inside a trait. The 550-file sample never reached it, which is why the full-extent run is a separate gate and not a bigger version of the same one.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-30): a signature's parameter declares, and the guard climbs to the owning function and skips when that owner is a `function_signature_item` — the same absence-of-a-body rule as the fn-pointer type, one level up. The fixture row also needed a second correction to be falsifiable at all: the first version forbade `uses -> on_stdout_line` WITHOUT importing that name, so the read could never resolve and the forbid row was vacuous (R12's lesson — an expectation cannot assert an absence the fixture does not set up). With `use helper::on_stdout_line;` added, disabling the guard makes the row fire (`uses[exec->on_stdout_line]`) and the fixture fails, which is the pre-fix proof. Mutant rust/reemit-signature-param-reads CAUGHT. FULL-EXTENT RESULT AFTER THE FIX: 167,088 relationships over 2,598 files, seven labels, 0 line-less and 0 off-name.

decisions.node_type: n/a — the CENSUS, and the four times IT was wrong
decisions.question: RUST-MR: the declaration census produced four findings that were not analyzer defects, and the pattern is the finding. (1) Wrong CHANNEL: `use` and `extern crate` were scored on 'is there a symbol on this line' when the lane's contract puts module dependencies in `imports`, so `extern crate` read 0/18 while doing exactly what `use` does. (2) Wrong PLACEHOLDER TEST: seven `Unknown` symbols were flagged as invented sentinels when six are enum variants literally NAMED `Unknown` and one is a field named `unknown`; a placeholder is a name ABSENT from the source. (3) Wrong DENOMINATOR: two `const _` declarations (R12: a blank name declares nothing) stayed in the denominator and made `const` read 99.7% when every real declaration was covered. (4) Wrong ID KEY: duplicate (name, line_start) pairs were labelled 'store id collisions' when `brain_symbol`'s primary key is `id TEXT` and no unique index covers that pair — consumer lookup ambiguity, not a constraint violation. Every correction was to the INSTRUMENT; the analyzer changed for none of them.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-30): the census now measures each form on the channel its contract uses (symbol for ten forms, `imports` for two), tests a placeholder by ABSENCE from the source, keeps declared-silent classes out of the denominator and reports them in their own buckets (R12 blanks; all-glob use trees — 292 sites, the lane's registered recall gap), and labels the (name, line) figure as consumer ambiguity. FULL EXTENT, 2,598 files, 1,016 walked: every live form 100.0% (fn 14409, struct 1705, enum 428, trait 133, mod 1009, type alias 789, const 591, static 92, macro_rules 265, extern crate 18, use 7450), `union` with no live site, 0 non-deterministic files, 0 placeholders, 0 ownerless members. Two of the four corrections were themselves bugs of the kind the elixir lane already catalogued — an identity comparison on a web-tree-sitter node (which returns a fresh wrapper per access, so `===` never matches) and a `childForFieldName('name')` read on a `const_item`, whose name is a bare identifier child and not a named field. The general rule this earns, which the elixir lane's census earned independently: a coverage table is only as trustworthy as the channel, the denominator, the name test and the key it is scored on, and each of those four was wrong here before the table was right.

decisions.node_type: n/a — the INSTRUMENT at corpus scale, and the corpus itself
decisions.question: RUST-MR: the corpus grew to rust-lang/rust's own src/ — 7,773 more .rs files, and the largest single .rs is only 0.7 MB — and every single-process sweep DIED on it. Not on one pathological file: bisected to a threshold, 4,000 files clean, 5,000 files abort in ts_parser__reduce -> ts_stack__iter -> ts_malloc_default, and ALL 7,773 files parse perfectly when parsed one at a time. So the pinned grammar's wasm heap is never released between parses in one process. The consequence is worse than the crash: these tools print their report at the END, so exhaustion produces NO OUTPUT AT ALL and reads exactly like 'this corpus has no data'. Two questions: is this a product defect, and what is the rule it earns for every future corpus?
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-30) — and the first fix was the WRONG one, which is the part worth keeping. Initial diagnosis: the wasm heap is not released between parses, so recycle the parser every 1,500 files. Recycling alone did NOT fix it — rustc still aborted. Growth curve (RSS per 250 files) separated the two hypotheses: monotonic climb 375 -> 491 -> 936MB (retention) versus sawtooth (coarse interval). It was retention. web-tree-sitter allocates each Tree in the wasm heap and only `tree.delete()` returns it; there is no finalizer, so one un-deleted tree per file accumulates until ts_malloc cannot grow the wasm memory. MEASURED AFTER `tree.delete()` in a finally: RSS 311 -> 149 -> 103 -> 98MB and FLAT across thousands of files — past the ~5,000-file abort threshold that killed the corpus. So: (1) explicit tree release, NOT parser recycling — recycling was treating the symptom, and had the growth curve not been printed, the second wrong fix would have shipped with the first; (2) both single-process instruments (the census parses twice per file, so both trees) now release in a finally; (3) the corpus and SCOPE grew with it — rust-lang/rust added, and `tests`, `test`, `benches` and `examples` are no longer skipped by the line audit or the census, because those are where macro_rules takes its strangest forms and where a declaration-position bug hides most easily, and an audit that skips them audits a corpus nobody ships. New extent: 13,101 real .rs files (rust 10,505 / cargo 1,372 / tokio 807 / serde 208 / ripgrep 110 / hyper 99). (4) Production was read before the claim was made and is immune by design: parallel-indexer's worker `exit` handler respawns the worker and re-routes its batch through handleWorkerTimeout, and a fresh worker's fresh heap succeeds — so the cost there is one respawn per exhausted worker, never a lost file. (5) RULE that generalizes past rust: a tool that prints its report at the END turns exhaustion into SILENCE, so every sweep must print the count it walked beside the count it intended.

decisions.node_type: n/a - the ORACLE, and the two dead ends that produced the right one
decisions.question: RUST-MR: at 1.35M relationships over rustc the M60 line audit reported 8 violations. All 8 were verified edge by edge and the ANALYZER was right every time - the name token is on the line the edge names. The five hand-written site walkers in the audit were stale on five syntax shapes at once: a macro invocation inside a macro_rules! body (mir.rs:628), a Self::method path (range.rs:286), an #![warn(...)] attribute (miri/lib.rs:52), a where-clause bound (iterator.rs:4163), and a qualified trait on a NEGATIVE impl (rustfmt/tests/source/negative-impl.rs:3). So the instrument was the defect. The question is what replaces it, because a proxy that must be TAUGHT each new syntax shape is the wrong tool for the claim 'the edge names the line of the node that bears its name'.
decisions.resolution: RULED (2026-09-30): the primary oracle is a TOKEN SET built from the parse tree - every identifier-shaped node in the file, as `name|line`. Completeness here means enumerating TOKENS, not contexts: a name-bearing token is always an identifier-shaped node, so the set is complete by construction, needs no per-shape knowledge, and inherits the grammar for free. The walkers are kept and DEMOTED to a reported cross-check, because an instrument that silently absorbs disagreement is how a stale instrument hides. Result on cargo+serde+hyper+ripgrep at full extent (218,290 relationships): 0 violations, 201,725 confirmed by the token oracle, and 0 confirmed only by the walkers - the token oracle subsumes them completely, which is what retiring a proxy should look like. TWO DEAD ENDS ARE PART OF THE RULING, because both nearly produced a false finding. (1) A lexical oracle over raw text needed a Rust-aware comment masker, and this corpus is full of URLs: the string "sparse+http://{}/index/" swallowed the .unwrap() on its own line, turning 80 correct edges into misses - and I was one step from filing a ruling about multi-line method chains on the strength of my own bug. (2) A hand-written per-file scanner then dropped 11 lines of a 182-line file, because a backslash escape consumes the newline after it, which made every name after them unverifiable. The transferable lesson: to check a claim the PARSER already knows, do not hand-roll a lexer - ask the tree. Also counted rather than excused: 72,382 of those edges come from files the grammar cannot fully parse (cargo's str![[...]] in tests/, the documented gap). Their LINES are still token-checked, but their LABELS come from a tree containing error nodes, which is where label semantics are least trustworthy - a third of the audited edges, and the largest remaining coverage hole in the lane.
